metadata.label: Shape model
metadata.coverage: Published PDS shape model, including poorly constrained source estimates. Both views use the gray grid for source-flagged poorly constrained regions. Source constraints keeps solid gray for stereo control and blue for limb silhouettes. Grid regions lack those constraints; they are not necessarily wholly unobserved. These are evidence categories, not surface colors. The combined model pole is retained at RA 255°, Dec +64.5°. Rotational phase is arbitrary and held fixed; no encounter or current rotation reconstruction is claimed.

metadata.label: Deep Impact · 2005
metadata.coverage: Photographs taken as the impactor approached Tempel 1, before the collision. Wider views surround a closer view of the impact region. The gray grid marks gaps; the original shadows remain.

metadata.label: Stardust-NExT · 2011
metadata.coverage: Stardust returned six years after Deep Impact. These photographs show a different encounter and viewing direction, rather than a direct before-and-after comparison. Original shadows remain; the gray grid marks gaps.

celestial.sunSource: JPL Horizons osculating elements; PDS source orientation held at arbitrary phase.

controls.label: Source constraints
controls.notes: Shape measurements mapped onto the nucleus. Solid gray marks stereo measurements, blue marks limb outlines, and the grid marks poorly constrained regions.

controls.label: Shape model
controls.notes: The published nucleus shape, simplified for display. Gray is a model material; the grid marks regions with weaker shape constraints.

controls.label: Deep Impact · 2005
controls.notes: Eight images follow Deep Impact’s approach in 2005. The closest views reveal finer ridges and depressions within the earlier photographs. Original shadows remain; the grid marks gaps or uncertain shape.

controls.label: Stardust-NExT · 2011
controls.notes: Stardust returned to Tempel 1 six years after Deep Impact. The photographs retain their original shadows; viewing differences limit comparisons with 2005. The gray grid marks gaps.

controls.label: Color temperature
controls.notes: False colors show the temperature fitted to infrared emission. Warm patches within each pixel dominate this measurement. Placement on the shape is approximate; the grid marks gaps.

controls.label: Infrared slope
controls.notes: False colors show how quickly reflected sunlight becomes brighter toward longer infrared wavelengths. Higher values mean a redder spectrum. Placement on the shape is approximate; the grid marks gaps. This does not measure terrain slope or identify minerals.
